name: Remote Access Tools
description:
An adversary may use legitimate remote access tools to establish an interactive command and control channel within a network. Remote access tools create a session between two trusted hosts through a graphical interface, a command line interaction, a protocol tunnel via development or management software, or hardware-level access such as KVM (Keyboard, Video, Mouse) over IP solutions. Desktop support software (usually graphical interface) and remote management software (typically command line interface) allow a user to control a computer remotely as if they are a local user inheriting the user or software permissions. This software is commonly used for troubleshooting, software installation, and system management.(Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)(Citation: CrowdStrike 2015 Global Threat Report)(Citation: CrySyS Blog TeamSpy) Adversaries may similarly abuse response features included in EDR and other defensive tools that enable remote access.

Remote access tools may be installed and used post-compromise as an alternate communications channel for redundant access or to establish an interactive remote desktop session with the target system. It may also be used as a malware component to establish a reverse connection or back-connect to a service or adversary-controlled system.

Installation of many remote access tools may also include persistence (e.g., the software's installation routine creates a [Windows Service](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003)). Remote access modules/features may also exist as part of otherwise existing software (e.g., Google Chrome’s Remote Desktop).(Citation: Google Chrome Remote Desktop)(Citation: Chrome Remote Desktop)

strategies.name: Behavior-Chain Detection for Remote Access Tools (Tool-Agnostic)

analytics.name: Analytic 1366
analytics.guidance: Chain of remote access tool behavior: (1) initial execution of remote-control/assist agent or GUI under user context; (2) persistence via service or autorun; (3) long-lived outbound connection/tunnel to external infrastructure; (4) interactive control signals such as shell or file-manager child processes spawned by the RAT parent.

tuning.description: Correlation period binding start→persistence→egress→child (default 15m, adjust per environment).
Differentiate help-desk/jump hosts and admin accounts from standard endpoints.
Known-good remote support tools; suppress expected events while still correlating anomalous sequences.
Alert when services/agents execute from user-writable or temp paths.
Vendors’ support clouds/CDNs to reduce false positives on egress detection.
Define which child shells from GUI parents are acceptable versus suspicious.
Thresholds for session duration, connection counts, and bytes_out/bytes_in ratio.

analytics.name: Analytic 1367
analytics.guidance: Sequence of RAT agent execution, systemd persistence, and long-lived external egress; optional interactive shells spawned from the agent.

tuning.description: Bind exec→service→egress events; extend for staged deployments.
Approved .service names/paths to avoid flagging corporate agents.
Define shells/interpreters considered anomalous when spawned by GUI/agent parents.
Flow heuristics for long-lived, client-heavy connections post-install.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve: Agent/headless flags (listen/connect/reverse/tunnel) or remote-control binaries spawning shells

log_sources.name: auditd:PATH
log_sources.channel: WRITE: Drop of binaries/scripts in ~/.local, /tmp, or /opt tool dirs

analytics.name: Analytic 1368
analytics.guidance: Electron/GUI or headless RAT execution followed by LaunchAgent/Daemon persistence and persistent external connections; interactive children (osascript/sh/curl) spawned by parent.

log_sources.channel: Process exec of remote-control apps or binaries with headless/connect flags

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures may be able to prevent traffic to remote access services.

mitigations.name: Limit Hardware Installation
mitigations.description: Block the use of IP-based KVM devices within the network if they are not required.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.description: Properly configure firewalls, application firewalls, and proxies to limit outgoing traffic to sites and services used by remote access software.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.description: Use application control to mitigate installation and use of unapproved software that can be used for remote access.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Consider disabling unnecessary remote connection functionality, including both unapproved software installations and specific features built into supported applications.

dependencies.description: NetSupport must be downloaded and exist on the disk at the specified location. (#{NetSupport_Path})

candidates.name: RustDesk Files Detected Test on Windows
candidates.description:
An adversary may attempt to trick the user into downloading RustDesk and use this to maintain access to the machine. 
Download of RustDesk installer will be at the destination location when successfully executed.

installer_path.description: where the installer will be downloaded to or already is located

dependencies.description: RustDesk must exist on disk at the specified location (#{installer_path})

candidates.name: RemotePC Software Execution
candidates.description:
An adversary may attempt to trick the user into downloading RemotePC Software for use as a C2 channel. 
Upon successful execution, RemotePC will be executed.

dependencies.description: RemotePC must exist on disk at the specified location (#{RemotePC_Path})

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
